description:
Parent: fz-go4.22. RESOLVED at main 417c5b0b5 -- no flake observed.

## What this reported

`matrix::tail_recursion::interp` was an ACTIVE (non-deferred, non-ignored) test
that flaked even single-threaded and in isolation: observed passing 2/2 then
failing 2/2 in the same session, on both a worktree and a pristine checkout at
d49562986 (2026-07-04). Suspected to be the .28.6 schedule-dependence family.

## What is true now

    for i in 1..10: cargo test --test fixture_matrix -- --test-threads=1 tail_recursion
    ok ok ok ok ok ok ok ok ok ok

Ten consecutive single-threaded runs, all green, all three lanes each time.

Closed on the absence of a flake. Note that the suspected root was
schedule-dependence, and the compiler's job schedule is now DETERMINISTIC by
construction (fz-f98.19: a job's fact emission order is preserved end to end, so
two compiles of the same input run the same jobs in the same order, pinned by
`compiling_the_same_root_twice_runs_the_same_jobs_in_the_same_order`). If the
diagnosis was right, that removed the mechanism.

Ten runs cannot prove a flake is gone. If it returns, reopening is cheap -- but
reopen with the two divergent outcomes captured (wrong-answer flip vs
pass/crash flip), which the original ticket asked for and never got.
title: tail_recursion::interp is flaky (non-deterministic pass/fail) even single-threaded in isolation
